correctness.rationale: Under 0<theta<pi and S in [0,1], D=1-2E[S(1-S)](1-cos theta)>0. Isotropic feature covariance equals (r^2 D/2)I, yielding unique all-real-matrix least-squares minimizer. Exact covariance and Pythagorean identities give the residual proportional to Var S, and differentiating the angular coefficient gives a single cosine zero for q<1/4, with the deterministic-midpoint boundary handled separately. Taylor expansion gives necessary and sufficient mean=1/2 and variance=1/12 for full O(h^4) generator recovery. Rational arithmetic checker verifies exact normal equations, risk and coefficients over extensive offset laws/angles; finite tests corroborate rather than prove universal statements.

originality.rationale: The full-text motivating article gives the uniform stochastic chord objective, bias–variance identity and second-order general loss consistency but no arbitrary-offset-law planar-rotation minimizer or exact risk/frequency/damping moment phase diagram. Lele and Li–Li–Liao contain the exact uniform-law fourth-order compact derivative symbol (including its easily deduced fold): this special Fourier statement is explicitly credited, not treated as original. Lu–Tsai studies rollout integrator-fitting, not stochastic chord-velocity regression. Two relevant full-text public records on trigonometric SBP and oscillator reachability have different objects and do not imply the joint statistical regression classification. A historical equivalent formulated as complex linear regression may exist outside indexed searches.
residual_risks: Published classical compact difference results cover the uniform imaginary response; no standalone novelty is attributed to that response or its fold.

The general all-law linear least-squares formula might be present as an unindexed corollary in older gradient-matching or flow-matching literature; indexed and full-text comparisons cannot prove its historical absence.

Lele primary PDF was read through an accessible textual rendering; its page screenshots could not be fetched, so visual equation inspection used the full open Wiley article as an independent corroboration.

value.rationale: The exact phase diagram resolves how to choose collocation distributions for an oscillatory inverse-ODE problem, a question raised by the motivating source. It separates preservation of conservation (offset mean), irreducible training loss (variance), fourth-order learned generator (two prescribed moments) and the unavoidable loss of monotone angular response above 2pi/3 for fourth-order laws. A deterministic midpoint gives zero loss and no interior angular fold but only second-order frequency recovery. This is a motivated structural distinction beyond routine mere parameter substitutions.
